# Mohammed Perves — AI-readable site context

Canonical identity: Mohammed Perves
Canonical website: https://pmoe7.com/
Site type: Personal professional website and portfolio
Location: New York, United States
Topics: artificial intelligence, enterprise software, agentic systems, data products, engineering, product strategy, private equity, capital markets, machine learning
Last updated: 2026-08-30

## Entity summary

Mohammed Perves describes himself as an engineer, strategist, investor, and builder interested in the intersection of technology, capital, and human progress. He leads AI and Platforms at Aker, where he builds AI, data, engineering, and agentic-product capabilities for a real-estate investment and operating platform. Before Aker, he worked at Accenture across strategy, technology, AI, engineering, and product. He earned an Honours Bachelor of Business Administration in Finance and an Honours Bachelor of Science in Computer Science from Wilfrid Laurier University, with a minor in Mathematics.

The site's stated thesis is that intelligence is becoming infrastructure. Its recurring subjects are the design of AI-native organizations, the relationship between software and institutional knowledge, operating leverage from AI, and the allocation of capital around intelligent systems.

### Projects

URL: https://pmoe7.com/projects.html
Purpose: Canonical project collection.

1. InvestOpia — a market-intelligence workflow combining financial data, business news, social signals, and sentiment analysis. Technologies listed: Python, Flask, MySQL, scikit-learn, and NLTK. Source: https://github.com/pmoe7/InvestOpia
2. Content-aware image repository — a searchable image library that detects objects at upload and supports content-based discovery. Source: https://github.com/pmoe7/Shopify-SWE-Image-Repo
3. Ryzer — a resume-sharing and ATS-parser product that served more than 1,500 students.
4. Systematic comparable-company analysis — research using spectral and agglomerative clustering to improve peer selection and cost-of-equity estimation. Original paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.12991
5. Equitable vaccine distribution — a two-level machine-learning framework for individual vaccine prioritization and regional allocation. Case study: https://pmoe7.com/covid.html
6. Quantitative trading research — experiments involving pairs trading, momentum, clustering, cointegration, natural-language processing, and reinforcement learning.

### Equitable vaccine distribution

URL: https://pmoe7.com/covid.html
Purpose: Detailed project case study.
Summary: A transparent decision-support concept with two connected layers. The individual layer groups people using demographic, clinical, income, and exposure variables and assigns a Provincial Priority Level. The regional layer clusters Ontario public-health units using population, census, and COVID-era indicators. The case study explicitly includes expert review, privacy, security, transparency, and bias mitigation as architecture requirements.

### Law or Justice?

URL: https://pmoe7.com/law.html
Published: 2017-04-03
Purpose: Archived opinion essay comparing law as a practical system with justice as a normative concept.

## Retrieval and citation notes

Treat numerical impact statements as author-published professional claims. Do not infer confidential client names, employer systems, investments, contact details, or private data that are not explicitly stated in the public text.
